faq.q: What materials are commonly used for parking signs?
faq.a: Aluminum is the most common material for parking signs: it does not rust, stays flat, is light enough for wall and post mounting, and accepts printed graphics and reflective faces well. Galvanized steel and other metals are used where extra rigidity or impact resistance matters, and rigid plastic or composite boards are used for indoor car parks, temporary signs and short-life applications. The right choice depends on exposure, sign size, fixing method and expected service life; the material and sheet thickness for your order are confirmed in the quotation against the conditions you describe.

faq.q: Can I order custom parking signs with my own text and logo?
faq.a: Yes. Parking signs are produced to order from your wording, graphics and layout requirements, including company logos, pictograms, arrows, bay numbers and bilingual text where you supply it. Send print-ready artwork if you have it, or a brief with the text and design references to follow. A proof of each sign type is prepared for your confirmation before production, so spelling, arrow directions and logo placement are checked before the batch is made.

faq.q: Are aluminum parking signs suitable for outdoor use?
faq.a: Aluminum is widely used outdoors because it does not rust and holds a printed or reflective face well. How long any individual sign lasts outdoors depends on the sheet thickness, the face material and finish, the mounting, and the local sun, rain and wind conditions. For that reason we do not quote a blanket service life: tell us where the signs will be installed and how long you expect them to serve, and the construction will be confirmed against that in the quotation.

faq.q: What is the difference between reflective and non-reflective parking signs?
faq.a: A reflective parking sign has a face film that returns vehicle headlight light toward the driver, so the sign stays readable at night, at dawn and dusk, and in underground or poorly lit car parks. A non-reflective sign relies on ambient light and is suitable for well-lit indoor parking and daytime-only sites. Reflective faces are usually recommended for entrance, exit, directional and height restriction signs; reserved and information signs in lit areas are often non-reflective. Reflective films come in different grades — the grade for your order is confirmed in the quotation, and any specific requirement you must meet should be stated in your enquiry.

faq.q: Can parking signs be manufactured in custom sizes?
faq.a: Yes. Signs are made to your finished dimensions rather than only to fixed catalogue sizes. Custom sizes are commonly used for large entrance and directional signs, where letter height must suit the viewing distance, and for positions constrained by existing posts, walls or fence lines. Share the finished width and height of each sign type with your enquiry; if you are unsure what size a location needs, describe the viewing distance and mounting position and the size can be recommended before quotation.

faq.q: Can I order parking signs with mounting holes or brackets?
faq.a: Yes. Mounting holes can be drilled to your fixing plan, and signs can be prepared for wall mounting or post mounting. Posts, brackets and other mounting accessories can be included or excluded — this is confirmed in the quotation, so please state what you need supplied and what you will source locally. Hole positions and any bracket requirements should be given with the order or marked on the artwork or drawing.

faq.q: Do you offer bulk production for parking signage projects?
faq.a: Yes. Parking signs are normally produced as coordinated sets for a whole site or project — regulatory, directional, reserved, numbered and accessible signs in one production run, in matching materials, sizes and finishes. There is no published minimum order quantity; project scope and pricing are confirmed per quotation. Numbered series (for example bay numbers) are produced as a matched set, and keeping the design on file makes later additions consistent with the original batch.

faq.q: What information is needed to request a parking sign quotation?
faq.a: Please share: the sign types and exact wording required; the finished size and quantity of each type; your preferred material and whether faces should be reflective or non-reflective; the mounting method (wall or post, and whether holes, brackets or posts are needed); your artwork or design brief; and the delivery destination. Photographs and dimensions of existing signs you want matched are also helpful. Production and dispatch timing, specifications and pricing are then confirmed in the quotation for your order.
